payload.name: Preserve Enumerated Items in Extracted Recommendations
payload.description: When a source message explicitly lists concrete items within a recommendation or offer and a memory candidate would collapse them into a generic phrase, use this Skill to keep each named item.
content: If a source message explicitly enumerates concrete items as part of a recommendation or offer (for example, 'acrylic paints, brushes, a canvas/paper, and a palette'), preserve each named item in the memory candidate as a compact list. Do not replace the enumeration with a generic placeholder such as 'supplies' that loses answerable facts.
Include only items explicitly stated in the message; do not infer additional items. If the candidate already contains the full enumeration, do not modify it. Stop once the named items are captured.

solves: Extraction candidates sometimes reduce an explicit item list to a generic phrase (e.g., 'recommend supplies'), making later questions about which specific items were recommended unanswerable. This Skill applies when a future session contains a message where one speaker recommends or offers concrete enumerated items and a memory candidate is being built from it; the candidate must keep each named item. It does not apply when the message only mentions a category or topic without enumerating concrete items, or when the generic phrase already reflects the full content.
